findings.location: examples/done/README.md:21 (section 1 Ideal, the `provenance` row, Evidence column)
findings.evidence: The Evidence cell attributes to `FILE:docs/litmus/questionnaire.json#provenance.future_state` the quote "carries an attestation in the published statement format, wrapped in the published envelope, whose subject is named by cryptographic digest". The questionnaire's provenance future_state text reads "wrapped in the published **signing** envelope". The word is dropped only here: the same README cell quotes it correctly twelve words earlier in its own middle column, and `grep -rn 'wrapped in the published envelope'` over the repository returns this one line. Mechanically checked two ways: of the 71 id- and FILE-attributed quotes in README.md, provenance.json, units/ and entries/, this is the only one that is not a substring of the record it names (docs/night/hidden/done.sh h-02); and the area's own test.sh section 16 catches it, which is why the shipped suite prints `passed 62, failed 1` and exits 1. This is the row the `provenance` litmus section is scored against, and the README's own opening rule (lines 12-15) is that every row is cited with a verbatim quote grepped back by section 16.
findings.fix: Restore the word: "wrapped in the published signing envelope". One character class of edit; the suite then prints passed 63, failed 0.

findings.location: examples/done/README.md:81 (section 4 What the user sees, the last row, `The outcome tiers`)
findings.evidence: The row says nothing the table does not already say and says it in vocabulary the repository does not use. It restates the first row of the same table and the `the ladder, not the word` row of section 1 with every term renamed - the ladder becomes "outcome tiers" and "completion tiers", the rungs become "those with all checks passing", `behavioural_run` becomes "behavioral activity" - which is exactly what docs/reference/ontology.md's success ladder and the context-75 vocabulary rule forbid: neither "outcome tier" nor "completion tier" appears anywhere else in the repository, and "behavioral" (American spelling) appears in no other line of this example while `behavioural` appears in run.py, test.sh, units/ and the cited record. Its Evidence is the same `FILE:docs/consumption/unit-design.md#checks` quote the row above it carries, and that quote ("a report whose behavioural_run is 0 is inconclusive, never passed") supports a rule about one rung, not a three-tier taxonomy - a citation that does not decide the sentence it is attached to. Nothing in run.py computes a "tier": close_unit() assigns `task success`, `candidate completion` or `none` (run.py:220-231).
findings.fix: Delete the row. Sections 1 and 4 already carry the ladder with the ontology's own words; if a summary row is wanted, name the three rungs and cite docs/reference/ontology.md#success-is-a-ladder-never-one-word as the section-1 row does.

findings.evidence: The closure declares four gate rules and README section 6 sells the extension point as "add or remove a rule in `promotion.gate_rules`", but only two of the four are read at the decision. `gate()` tests `"attested-subject-required" in rules` and `"run-output-predicate-required" in rules`; `subject-digest-must-match` and `statement-must-verify` never appear on the right of an `in rules` - they are only labels in the fallback at run.py:356-358, chosen from the verification result. Falsified: with `subject-digest-must-match` removed from the declaration, `--break mutate-subject` still refuses, still names `subject-digest-must-match`, and now names a rule the closure does not declare - `{'with': (2, 0, 'subject-digest-must-match', declared=True), 'without': (2, 0, 'subject-digest-must-match', declared=False)}` (docs/night/hidden/done.sh h-07). test.sh section 6 asserts `rule in decided[0]["gate_rules"]` ("the rule that decided is not one the closure declared") and passes only because the shipped declaration happens to list all four; the differential in that same section varies exactly the one rule that is read, and the row generalises from it to all four. The rules are also attested: predicate.invocation.decision_refs is built as `gate:{rule}` for every declared rule (run.py:322), so two of the four decision references in every statement name rules that decided nothing.
findings.fix: Read each declared rule where it decides - build TrustPolicy's expected_subjects only when `subject-digest-must-match` is declared, and make signature/expiry verification conditional on `statement-must-verify` - then extend section 6's differential to remove each of the four rules in turn and assert the four arms differ. Where a rule genuinely cannot be switched off, drop it from the declaration and say in section 6 that the gate always applies it.

findings.location: examples/done/README.md:117 (run steps, row 1) and examples/done/provenance.json:60 (measured) and :110 (visible_checks_counted)
findings.evidence: Three files agree on a number the program does not print. Run-steps row 1 promises `bash examples/done/test.sh` -> `passed 63, failed 0`; FLOOR=63 (test.sh:15) and provenance.visible_checks_counted is 63. Executed as printed from the repository root, the suite prints `passed 62, failed 1` and exits 1, failing `every quote is pasted out of the record it cites, not remembered`. provenance.json's first measured bullet ("bash examples/done/test.sh prints 'passed 63, failed 0'") and its quote bullet ("every quote in README.md and in this file is grepped verbatim out of the record or the file it names") are therefore both false as shipped. Agreement between test.sh, provenance.json and the README is not evidence - the area's own section 17 check compares the three numbers to each other and never to the suite's real last line, so the one check that would have caught this is the one that was not written.
findings.fix: Fix R75DONE-001, then re-run and paste the real last line. Add to section 17 an assertion that runs the suite's own printed last line against FLOOR (or move that assertion outside test.sh, as docs/night/hidden/done.sh h-11 does), so a count in three files is checked against the program rather than against itself.

findings.evidence: The closure declares `"full_predicate": "agent-action"` and `"light_predicate": "build"`. Neither name is read anywhere: `grep -n 'full_predicate\|light_predicate' run.py test.sh harnesses.py` returns nothing, and the predicate types come from the two interface constants `self.prov_iface.PREDICATE_AGENT_ACTION` and `PREDICATE_BUILD` (run.py:264-271). Falsified: swapping full_predicate for the declared light_predicate value leaves both arms emitting exactly the same two predicate types (docs/night/hidden/done.sh h-08). Section 6's extension-points table has no row for them and section 6's gap table has no carried-and-not-consumed row for them either - the one field this example does write up that way is `payload.recurrence` (G9), which is the pattern these two should follow if they are not going to be read.
findings.fix: Either resolve the two declared names to the interface's predicate-type URIs at the point the predicate type is chosen and add a differential arm proving it, or delete both members from the closure. If they are kept unread on purpose, add a gap row with a research query as G9 does for recurrence.

findings.location: examples/done/run.py:180-190 (Close.identity_chain) and README.md:57 (section 3, the schedule row)
findings.evidence: `obtained_via` is read only for the root hop (`declared[-1]`, run.py:171-176). For every other declared hop the loop keeps the actor and drops the rest - `above = [hop["actor"] for hop in reversed(declared[:-1])]` (run.py:180) - and then presents each hop with the literal `"direct"` (run.py:187-188), after which the binding stamps `token_exchange` on it. entries/schedule.json declares the schedule hop as `"obtained_via": "workload_attestation"` (the third value the published entry schema's enum allows), and README section 3 sells that door as "`schedule:nightly-close-sweep` attested" in its own What is different column - but out/schedule.jsonl's identity-resolved record shows that hop as `"obtained_via": "token_exchange"`, so the artifact contradicts the row. test.sh section 10's `chains.log` reads the hop actors and never the declared obtained_via, and its identity-root differential varies only `delegation_chain[-1]`, so no check touches the value.
findings.fix: Present each declared hop with the `obtained_via` the envelope declares, so the schedule door's attested hop is issued as attested and the external door's exchanged hops as exchanged, and extend the section-10 differential to vary a non-root hop's obtained_via and assert the hop_trace moves. If a non-root value cannot be honoured by these bindings, say so in the gap table and stop describing the schedule door as attested.

findings.evidence: `HOP_LIFETIMES` is a literal four-tuple and is indexed by hop number: `scope, lifetime = ladder[i], HOP_LIFETIMES[i]`. The published entry schema puts no upper bound on `actor.delegation_chain` (minItems 1, no maxItems). A document with five declared hops - schema-valid, checked with examples/end-to-end/run.py's own validator - reaches `IndexError: tuple index out of range` and exits 1 with a Python traceback, not `application/problem+json` and exit 2 (docs/night/hidden/done.sh h-09). The four shipped entries declare one, two, two and three hops, so no shipped declaration reaches the path; a reader's does. This breaks the row this area cites twice - `F-b4-07` "Typed and machine-readable. Never parsed from prose" - and section 4's "one refusal shape reaching the caller".
findings.fix: Compute the lifetime from the root's lifetime and the hop index (each hop a declared fraction shorter than the one before) so the ladder is as long as the declaration, exactly as `narrow_ladder()` already computes the scope ladder from two declarations rather than writing one down; or refuse a chain longer than the ladder with a typed problem before any credential is issued. Add a probe entry with a deeper chain to test.sh section 10.

findings.location: examples/done/run.py:362-375 (Close.run) and run.py:595, README.md:79 ("What a refused closure still leaves")
findings.evidence: README section 4 promises unconditionally that a refused closure leaves "Every unit it did close, sealed, attested and appended, plus one `run-rejected` record naming the rule that stopped it. A refusal is recorded, not swallowed", cited to the concern-provenance future state "refused and failed units are attested as well as successful ones". Only refusals raised through `Close.refuse` reach that record: `run()` catches `Refusal` and writes run-rejected, while a capability's own typed Problem propagates past it to main()'s `except close.problems` handler (run.py:595), which prints and exits 2 having written nothing. Reached with the failure path the provenance binding already publishes: `PROVENANCE_FAIL=1 python3 run.py --entry entries/human.json` refuses 503 adapter-unavailable after the entry was admitted and leaves a receipt reading `['entry-admitted', 'identity-resolved', 'unit-closed', 'subject-sealed']` - no run-rejected line, and one more subject sealed than attested (docs/night/hidden/done.sh h-10). test.sh measures three refusals, all three of them `Refusal`-shaped, so the section that would fail is not written.
findings.fix: Record run-rejected for any typed refusal once the publisher exists - wrap `closure_run()` so `self.problems` is handled on the same path as `Refusal` - and add a section asserting the record after a capability refusal (PROVENANCE_FAIL=1 is already the binding's published failure path). Either way the sealed and attested counts on one receipt should never diverge.

findings.evidence: "the entry envelope's own digest is a material of every statement, so no two doors produce the same one (`test.sh` section 1)" is a claim about every statement proved over one statement per door. Each door writes four statements - one full run-output statement into out/attestations-<door>.jsonl and three metadata-light ones through the wired boundary into <prov-root>/attestations.jsonl - and section 1's check reads only the first file. Read back out of the artifacts: of 21 statements a single pass over the four doors writes, 17 carry `code_version.scripts_sha256: {}` and `invocation.correlation.run_id: "n/a"`, and none of them carries an entry-envelope material (docs/night/hidden/done.sh h-06). So the section-1 row's future state - every artifact "is the subject of a signed statement" whose predicate names the code version, the inputs and the actor (F-b4-05) - holds for one of the four subjects per door, and the other three are attested to an artifact digest and an actor and nothing else. `X-maturity-c-024` justifies metadata-light as a cost trade, but the gap table has no row saying what the light record gives up.
findings.fix: Either pass the run's code version and correlation into `emit.attest_and_record` so a light statement is thin in materials but still names the run and the code that made it, or narrow the section-3 sentence to the run-output statement and add a gap row (with a research query) saying the metadata-light record names neither the code version nor the run, and what a verifier can therefore conclude from it.

findings.evidence: The note reads "nothing in this area re-hashes that tree (README gap G6)". G6 is "Promotion success is staged, not reached" (README.md:159); the source-tree gap is G7 (README.md:160). provenance.json's measured list claims "the gap table is keyed G1..G13 rather than by position" precisely so a reference survives renumbering, and test.sh's sections check covers only `test.sh section N` references, not gap ids, so nothing catches a G-reference that has drifted.
findings.fix: Point the note at G7, and extend the section-16 or section-17 walk to resolve every `G<n>` reference in the area's files against the gap table's own keys.

findings.evidence: The context-75 shape asks section 5 to show how the example is built "from units and the six operators". The table carries rows for sequence, bounded loop, judge and approval gate - judge as an explicit "none here" row - and no row at all for `parallel` or `agent call`. The three sibling areas that carry the same section account for all six (examples/run has six separate rows; examples/watch and examples/steer fold the unused ones into `parallel, bounded loop` and `judge, parallel` rows). A reader cannot tell whether the two missing operators were considered and not needed or simply not written (docs/night/hidden/done.sh h-04).
findings.fix: Add one row covering `parallel` and `agent call`, in the shape the judge row already uses: what it would be at this boundary and why the closure does not use it.

findings.evidence: Two smaller places where a claim is not backed by what runs. (a) provenance.json lists under `measured` the sentence "each declared value was falsified before its row was written: ignoring the materiality list, the redactable flag, the notify surface, the gate rules or the computed scope ladder turns that value's own section red and not merely the suite" - a claim about the author's process, not about anything test.sh executes; the boundary's rule is that anything the run does not measure sits under `claimed`, and R75DONE-003 shows the gate-rules half of the sentence is true for one of four rules. (b) `--identity-adapter`'s help text is "identity binding: dryrun" while sections 5 and 6 both sell a `second` (attested-workload) binding selected by that flag and test.sh section 14 runs it; section 17's argparse check compares flag names against `--help` and never the values, so a reader of `--help` alone cannot find the binding the README proves.
findings.fix: Move the falsification sentence to `claimed`, or replace it with the arms test.sh actually runs. Give --identity-adapter the same "dryrun or second" help text --prov-adapter has, and have the section-17 check assert that each adapter value the README names appears in --help too.

findings.evidence: `harnesses.state_external_verifier()` exists to give the independent verifier's path through the loader, and nothing calls it: test.sh writes the literal `"../../harness/state-persistence/verify_external.py"` at four sites (sections 8, 9 and 14). The area's own composition row says the point of harnesses.py is that this example calls rather than copies; a helper nobody calls and a path repeated four times is the reverse.
findings.fix: Call the helper from the four sites, or delete it.

findings.evidence: The dry-run attestation store is `out/attestations-<door>.jsonl`, keyed by the envelope's `kind` and independent of `--prov-root`, while the artifacts and the manifest go to `--prov-root` and the state objects to OBJSTORE_DIR - three roots for one period. The adapter truncates its file on construction (harness/provenance/adapters/dryrun.py:41), so two runs of the same door with different `--prov-root` values silently share and overwrite one envelope store: after a full `bash test.sh`, out/attestations-human.jsonl holds the statements of section 17's `--break mutate-subject` demo, not those of the section-1 run whose subject digests section 1 asserted over. Nothing measured depends on it today because section 1 reads the file before section 17 rewrites it, but the artifact left in the tree does not correspond to the check that read it.
findings.fix: Derive the dry-run store path from `--prov-root` (for example `<prov-root>/envelopes-<door>.jsonl`) so one flag names one period, and have section 1 re-read the file it asserted over at the end of the suite.

plants_caught.why: Single-site insertion with the shape row 75 has now seen in five areas: one word ('signing') dropped from a quote in the Ideal table's Evidence column, while the same file quotes the same sentence correctly twelve words earlier in the same cell and the phrase as written appears nowhere else in the repository. Found by the mechanical verbatim pass over all 71 id- and FILE-attributed quotes before anything else in the area was read, and independently confirmed by the area's own test.sh section 16 going red.

Single-site table row duplicating its neighbour's citation with every term renamed and a circular reason - the second half of the shape the ask, watch and steer plants took. 'outcome tier', 'completion tier' and the American 'behavioral' occur nowhere else in the repository or in this example; the row's Evidence is verbatim the row above it and supports a rule about one rung rather than the taxonomy the sentence asserts; and no code path computes a tier. It is not an authorial habit: the rest of the README uses the ontology's ladder vocabulary consistently, including two rows in the same table.

plants_note: Nominated on shape, not on count. The findings separated from these two are authorial: they repeat across sites (the gate-rules generalisation in run.py, test.sh and README section 6; the three-file agreement on 63) or have siblings (unread declared values beside full_predicate/light_predicate, obtained_via, recurrence), which is the pattern row 75 has used to tell a plant from a habit since the run review.
what_holds: The wired boundary is real and checkable: harness/provenance/emit.py is loaded by path and is the same module object examples/end-to-end/run.py and harness/linked/linked.py call, asserted on the loaded function's own __code__.co_filename rather than on a name (test.sh section 14).

Verification reads only the envelope: out/v/verify_alone.py chdirs to /, imports the interface by path, imports no adapter, and the falsified arm fails with subject_mismatches 1 - and the same verifier accepts the second attestation binding's statement.

The append-only history is checked by a verifier that imports nothing of the harness: an external subprocess recomputes the root the store returned at two doors, catches a mid-history edit at its index, and catches a truncated tail by the root rather than by the record chain; the compare-and-swap race lands one writer and refuses the other 409.

Six of the ten extension points are proved by a real differential that varies the declared value and asserts the two records differ (materiality, retention.redactable, promotion.kind, notify.surface, promotion.requires_scope, the root hop's obtained_via), and three adapter swaps run the whole closure rather than a probe.
The gate has both halves - no failure and a floor under the count - and a hollow copy of the suite exits non-zero against it.

provenance.cites is exactly the ids the rows carry in both directions, every REF- entry names a file that exists, and the eleven claimed lines are honest about what is not measured, including the held-out deciding check.
